context: a letter from W. E. Darwin, which you are answering
exchanges:
I send you the 3 kinds of Buckthorn. I went to the place yesterday, and marked some shrubs, there seemed about as many female trees, as there were of the other two put together   As soon as I have examined pollen etc of the two I will let you know.

Your affect son W E Darwin

very many thanks for Rhamnus, which I have so long wished to see.— As a species it seems one step less unisexual than Holly. It wd be interesting to know whether the male or Hermaphrodite flowers with rather longer pistil bear any fruit– As stamens are in female far more rudimentary than the pistil is in the male,, at least in the Hermaphrodite, flowers, the species probably once existed in state of Thyme, ie, some plants, hermaphrodite & some female, but none as pure males—

And this is just what I wanted to know— I see no evidence of its having once been dimorphic like Primula.—

You are the man to do a job thoroughily

Your affect Father | C. Darwin

Do not forget the white Broom.—

Thanks about N.W. R. Shares. I shall sell. I can get £113 for each share.—
